reason: Prioritize the active K-loop schedules: they preserve the four-tile design and ordered FP32 updates while testing load placement or loop control. The evidence contains no measured gain for these active-path changes. Panel packing and prefetch are next: they may improve operand access, but add timed work; the earlier distance-4 prefetch regressed on the inactive full512 path, which does not establish the outcome here. Scratch blocking and transpose fusion require more restructuring and may add loop or data movement costs. Padding has no demonstrated cache conflict and increases scratch use. The large B layout has higher packing and addressing costs. A transpose-only fallback change does not affect the fixed n=512 benchmark, so it ranks last.
